properties.natural_language: Before a block is accepted by the fork choice, all blob data referenced by KZG commitments must be retrieved and verified via verify_blob_kzg_proof_batch; blocks with unavailable blob data must not be added to the store.
The on_block handler must verify parent existence in the store, valid timing, and finalization lineage before asserting data availability; failure at any assertion must reject the block.
After a block passes all fork choice assertions including data availability, the block and resulting state must be added to the store and the block becomes a candidate for the fork choice head.

An attacker cannot selectively withhold blob data to cause honest nodes to disagree on block validity; if blob data is available to any honest node within the availability window, it must be available to all.
Extraneous or invalid blobs injected by an attacker must not prevent acceptance of otherwise-valid blocks; blob verification must match blobs to their block's KZG commitments.
PayloadAttributes sent to the execution engine must include the parent_beacon_block_root (EIP-4788) alongside timestamp, prev_randao, suggested_fee_recipient, and withdrawals.
Blocks that previously passed data availability checks retain their validity even after blob pruning past MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs.
A validator must check inclusion list committee assignment via get_inclusion_committee_assignment at each epoch boundary before constructing any inclusion list.
The execution engine's get_inclusion_list() response must be structurally valid; a compromised execution engine returning empty or manipulated lists undermines censorship resistance.
A signed inclusion list must be broadcast to the P2P network before the submission deadline (~67% into the slot), computed as slot_start + (slot_duration * 6700 / 10000).
The SignedInclusionList must include slot, validator_index, committee_root, transactions, and a BLS signature using DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE before broadcast.
For attestation duties, get_attester_head must be used instead of raw fork choice head; if the head block is IL-unsatisfied, the attester head returns the parent block root.
Attestations broadcast with IL-aware head votes must correctly reflect the attester head computation, not the raw fork choice head.
Block proposers must collect inclusion lists from the inclusion_list_store up to PROPOSER_INCLUSION_LIST_CUTOFF_BPS (~92% of previous slot) and include mandated transactions in the execution payload.

An attacker controlling a minority of inclusion list committee members must not be able to suppress honest members' inclusion list broadcasts; network-level attacks on committee members that suppress inclusion lists would allow unchecked proposer censorship.
The eth_getBlockByHash RPC response must include the baseFee field (in Quantity hex format) if and only if the queried block is at or after the EIP-1559 fork block.
The eth_getBlockByHash RPC response must NOT include the baseFee field for blocks before the EIP-1559 fork block.
When a block hash is not found in local storage, the JSON-RPC response must return a null result.
The baseFee value included in the response must be the authentic value from the block header; the client must have accurate knowledge of the EIP-1559 fork block number.
The baseFee field must be formatted as a hexadecimal Quantity string with '0x' prefix and no leading zeros (except for zero value itself).
For blocks at or after block number 13,773,000, difficulty calculation must use the Arrow Glacier offset of 10,700,000 subtracted from the actual block number for the bomb component.
The difficulty bomb component must be computed as 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2); when the fake block number is near zero due to the offset, this yields a negligible bomb effect.
Block difficulty validation must recompute the expected difficulty using Arrow Glacier rules and compare against the claimed header difficulty; mismatches must result in block rejection.
Blocks with invalid difficulty values must be rejected and not added to the chain; the rejection must propagate appropriately.
Fork activation must be deterministic: blocks before 13,773,000 use London rules and blocks at/after 13,773,000 use Arrow Glacier rules; all clients must agree on this boundary.
Arrow Glacier only modifies the difficulty bomb delay offset; all other protocol rules (EIP-1559 gas mechanics, gas limits, etc.) remain identical to the London fork.
An account is considered empty if and only if nonce=0, balance=0, and code is empty; storage state is not evaluated for emptiness determination.
Empty accounts must be deleted from the state trie at the end of transaction execution after all state changes have been applied.
All of the following operations must trigger an account 'touch' for emptiness evaluation: zero-value CALL, CREATE, zero-value SELFDESTRUCT, transaction target, and miner fee recipient.
After EIP-158, zero-value CALLs and SELFDESTRUCTs to nonexistent addresses must NOT charge the 25,000 gas account creation cost.
Contracts must not rely on the distinction between empty and nonexistent accounts for security logic; deletion of empty accounts changes behavior observable via EXTCODESIZE and similar opcodes.
During the transition period, attackers must not be able to profitably exploit cheap touches (~700 gas) of empty accounts to cause sustained state churn that increases uncle rates.
Beacon blocks received via gossip must have KZG commitment count validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; blocks exceeding this limit must be rejected.
For beacon_aggregate_and_proof messages, committee_bits must have exactly 1 bit set and the aggregate data index must equal 0.
SingleAttestation messages on beacon_attestation subnets must have data.index == 0 and the attester must be verified as a member of the committee for the given slot.
Blob sidecars on gossip subnets must have blob index and KZG commitments validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; exceeding limits must cause rejection.
BlobSidecarsByRange and BlobSidecarsByRoot requests must not return more than MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA sidecars; requests exceeding limits must receive an error response.
BeaconBlocksByRange and BeaconBlocksByRoot v2 responses must return fork-appropriate SignedBeaconBlock types, including electra.SignedBeaconBlock for blocks at or after the Electra fork epoch.
Peers must not send Deneb-format messages after the Electra fork epoch; strict fork version validation must be applied to prevent consensus divergence from incorrectly formatted messages.

The 9 blob sidecar subnets (BLOB_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT_ELECTRA) must provide sufficient distribution capacity for the increased Electra blob count; subnet congestion must not cause propagation delays that affect data availability.
An attacker must not be able to flood attestation subnets with valid-looking SingleAttestation messages faster than honest nodes can validate committee membership.
SingleAttestation messages that pass committee membership and data.index validation must be forwarded to other peers on the subnet.
JUMP must pop exactly one element from the stack and validate the destination against the pre-computed valid_jump_destinations set; destinations not in the set must raise InvalidJumpDestError.

JUMPI must pop destination and condition from stack; when condition != 0, the destination must be validated against valid_jump_destinations; when condition == 0, PC increments normally without destination validation.
JUMP must charge GAS_MID (8 gas) and JUMPI must charge GAS_HIGH (10 gas) before performing destination validation.
After a valid JUMP, evm.pc must be set to the jump destination address; after JUMPI with condition=0, evm.pc must be incremented by 1.
STOP must set evm.running = False and increment PC by 1, causing execution to halt normally.
The PC opcode must push the current program counter value to the stack and the GAS opcode must push the remaining gas (after charging GAS_BASE) to the stack; both charge GAS_BASE (2 gas).

The valid_jump_destinations set must be pre-computed by scanning bytecode before execution begins; the scan must correctly skip PUSH data bytes to avoid marking data containing 0x5b as valid destinations.
Attackers must not be able to create valid jump destinations at arbitrary bytecode addresses through data manipulation; the JUMPDEST scan must distinguish opcodes from PUSH data bytes.
InvalidJumpDestError must properly halt execution and consume all remaining gas; invalid jumps must not cause undefined behavior or partial execution.
JUMPDEST (0x5b) must charge GAS_JUMPDEST (1 gas) and serve only as a valid landing marker; it performs no state changes beyond gas charging and PC increment.

Type 1 transactions must have the 0x01 prefix byte; the RLP-decoded payload must contain exactly 11 fields including chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, and signature components.
Access list format must match [[{20 bytes}, [{32 bytes}...]...]...]; addresses must be exactly 20 bytes and storage keys exactly 32 bytes. Invalid formats must be rejected.
Signature verification must be performed over keccak256(0x01 || rlp([chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList])); invalid signatures must reject the transaction.
Intrinsic gas for access list transactions must include 2400 gas per address and 1900 gas per storage key in the access list, in addition to standard base gas (21000 + calldata costs).
After pre-warming, all access list addresses must be in accessed_addresses and all (address, key) tuples in accessed_storage_keys; subsequent SLOAD on prewarmed keys costs 100 gas (vs 2100 cold).
Duplicate entries in access lists must be charged gas (2400 per duplicate address, 1900 per duplicate key) but provide no additional warm access benefit; the gas cost is wasted.
Access set initialization must add sender, recipient, and all precompile addresses to accessed_addresses before processing the access list entries.
Transaction validation must check the chain ID matches the expected network; mismatched chain IDs must reject the transaction to prevent replay attacks.
Access list size is bounded only by block gas limit; attackers cannot use oversized access lists to cause processing time disproportionate to gas cost.
Access list address entries must be validated as exactly 20 bytes and storage keys as exactly 32 bytes; non-conforming lengths must fail validation.
DEVp2p version negotiation must complete during handshake before any compressed messages are processed; the minimum common version between peers determines compression use.
For DEVp2p v5 sessions, all message payloads must be Snappy compressed (no framing) before encryption; compression must not be applied for v4 sessions.
On the receive path, the Snappy decompressed size varint must be checked against 2^32-1 limit; varint overflow must terminate the connection.
Decompressed message size must be validated against the 16MB limit BEFORE decompression to prevent memory exhaustion; messages exceeding 16MB must be rejected without decompression.
An attacker must not be able to construct valid Snappy streams that bypass the size check but expand beyond the 16MB limit during decompression.
The Snappy library implementation must be free of buffer overflows and other memory safety vulnerabilities; malformed compressed data must not achieve remote code execution.
Successfully decompressed messages must be dispatched to the appropriate subprotocol handler (eth/les); decompression failures must result in message rejection and potential peer disconnection.
Nodes must have sufficient memory to buffer 16MB decompressed messages; concurrent large message processing must not cause memory exhaustion.

External resource origins must satisfy all three mandatory requirements before approval: unique revision identification (git hash, version, or date), proven availability history (~10 years), and free access.
Failure of any single mandatory requirement must result in origin rejection; there is no partial approval.
When an approved origin is found to violate requirements, it must be removed from the EIP-1 approved list; re-approval requires fixing the violation and undergoing re-evaluation.
External origins must not modify historical resource revisions after publication; if an origin alters previously published content, implementers could build against modified specifications.
EIP editors must consistently and fairly evaluate origin approval requests; inconsistent evaluation could lead to important origins being rejected or unreliable origins being approved.
Revision identification validation must accept at least one of: git commit hashes, version numbers, or publication dates as valid identification methods.
Ten years of availability is a strong benchmark for meeting longevity requirements but EIP editors have discretion for origins with shorter history if other factors demonstrate reliability.
EXT* opcodes (EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, EXTCODEHASH) on prewarmed addresses must cost 100 gas; on cold (non-listed) addresses must cost 2600 gas.
Blocks queued pending blob arrival have no guaranteed queuing behavior, timeout, or retry semantics; implementations may optionally queue but are not mandated to do so.
Before EIP-158, zero-value operations to nonexistent addresses charged 25,000 gas for account creation; after EIP-158 this cost is eliminated for zero-value operations.
The transition from empty accounts existing to all being cleared must eventually complete; the number of pre-existing empty accounts is finite.
Blob sidecars returned by BlobSidecarsByRange must include at least the first blob-carrying block's complete sidecar set or none; partial sidecar sets are treated as unavailable.
When no block arrives by ~67% minus 1000ms of the slot, the validator must use the local get_head() to proceed with inclusion list construction rather than waiting indefinitely.
The same baseFee inclusion rules that apply to eth_getBlockByHash should apply to eth_getBlockByNumber; both must correctly handle the EIP-1559 fork boundary.
After compression, the message size field must be updated to reflect the compressed payload length, not the original uncompressed length.
Message encryption via RLPx must be applied after compression for v5 sessions; the order is: compress -> update size -> encrypt -> send.
An attacker must not be able to exploit the predictable difficulty patterns created by the bomb delay for selfish mining advantage or timing attacks on block production.
Approved external resource origins must maintain availability and free access indefinitely; removal of access to referenced resources would break EIP specification references.
Re-evaluation of approved origins should occur on a best-effort basis or when community reports issues; no specification of mandatory re-evaluation frequency exists.
Free access means no monetary cost; registration or authentication requirements may be acceptable if no payment is required.
The RPC response must be ready and correctly formatted after either including or excluding the baseFee field based on fork status.
The baseFee field must never be included for pre-1559 blocks and must always be included for post-1559 blocks; there must be no ambiguous behavior at the fork boundary.
After collecting inclusion lists and extracting mandated transactions, the block proposer must include these transactions in the PayloadAttributes sent to the execution engine.
On the receive path, the order must be: decrypt -> check if decompression needed -> read varint -> validate size -> decompress -> dispatch. The size check must occur before decompression.
The 10% discount in access list gas pricing (2400 vs 2600 for addresses, 1900 vs 2100 for storage keys) must provide meaningful savings while covering the processing cost of access list entries.
The Merge (transition to Proof of Stake) is expected to occur before the delayed bomb becomes significant; if Merge is delayed, block times would increase requiring another bomb delay fork.
The network must be able to tolerate temporarily increased uncle rates during the transition period while empty accounts are being cleared.
After all access list entries are processed, the transaction is ready for EVM execution with all warm access sets populated.
The eth_getBlockByHash request accepts two parameters: block hash and full transaction flag; the block hash must be used for storage lookup.
Community members may propose new origins for approval; the proposal must be evaluated by EIP editors against all mandatory requirements.
Access list generation tools must produce correct and complete access lists; malicious or buggy tools could waste gas or miss critical storage accesses.
Subprotocol messages (eth/les) must be properly assembled before entering the compression pipeline; the message format must be valid RLP regardless of compression.
MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA must be computed as MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB * MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB is a fixed Deneb constant not modified by Electra.
Emptiness evaluation and deletion of touched accounts must occur at the end of transaction execution, after all state changes including CALL, CREATE, and SELFDESTRUCT have been applied.
Users or tools must be able to accurately predict which addresses and storage keys a transaction will access; inaccurate predictions waste gas on unused warm slots.
All Ethereum clients must upgrade to Arrow Glacier before block 13,773,000; non-upgraded clients will fork off the main chain due to difficulty calculation mismatch.
Empty accounts cannot be created faster than they are cleared; the state bloat reduction mechanism must converge to zero empty accounts over time.
Network latency must allow inclusion list committee members to receive blocks and broadcast their inclusion lists within the ~67% slot window; high latency would weaken censorship resistance.
